name: nm51
question: Does nm49 re-trained with the calling station restored to its old share of training (nm49's pool plus 2 more stations: 3 of 16 entries, about 19%, against nm25's 1 of 5) win back nm25's result against the station while keeping nm49's gains against the partner's aggressive and odd-sized players, without losing to anyone else?
why: nm49 (2026-11-28) passed every check but one: it beat the partner's players by more than nm25 (the bluffer by +16.65 [+15.78, +17.52], the jammer +1.40, raise5x +0.95, raise8x +0.73) but lost -13.28 [-13.98, -12.57] bb/100 of nm25's win against the calling station. Adding nine players cut the station from 1 of 5 pool entries to 1 of 14 (7%), and nm45 lost to the station the same way (-16.5) after its pool changed. The likely cause is dilution: against bluffers it learnt to call down and bluff more, which a player who never folds punishes. This run starts from nm49 (to keep its gains) and restores the station's share; the checks are nm49's, unchanged, all against nm25. Registered on 2026-11-28 to run after nm50.

checks.why: it must not lose to nm25 in nm25's own game

the point of the run: on the same deals as nm25, the 95% interval of the difference must lie above zero against each of the pool's kinds (raise3x left out: its size is nm25's own open, nothing new to learn)
nm49 failed here (station -13.28): with the station at 3 of 16 entries its win must come back to within 2.0 of nm25's (interval above -2.0 against each)
at least as good as nm25 on average across 25 generated players, and never far behind
bluff jams and raises must lose prize equity against it, as against nm25
as nm45 and nm47: the mean of four 30-minute exploiters, limit nm25's +0.75 plus 0.5; a network bent towards calling aggressive players is easier to exploit
